entries.043eb27645dbab56: This category manufactures and sells automotive parts through local subsidiaries in Thailand and Indonesia. The consolidated subsidiaries are four companies: H-ONE Parts (Thailand) Co., Ltd. (Ayutthaya Province) and H-ONE Parts Sriracha Co., Ltd. (Chonburi Province) in Thailand, and PT. H-ONE KOGI PRIMA AUTO TECHNOLOGIES INDONESIA and PT. RODA PRIMA AUTO TECHNOLOGIES INDONESIA (both in Karawang Regency) in Indonesia. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥18,332 million (¥25,722 million in the prior year), and segment profit (operating profit) was ¥2,138 million (¥96 million in the prior year). The company explains that, in addition to the effect of the transfer of its Indian subsidiary and a decline from the prior year in production of automobile frames for its main customers, revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥18,416 million, down 28.6% year on year; meanwhile, profit margins improved through structural reforms, including consolidation of manufacturing lines. H-ONE India PVT., Ltd. in India was included in this category until the prior year, but it was excluded from the scope of consolidation in March 2025, so it has not been included since the first-quarter consolidated accounting period of the fiscal year ended March 2026. There are 935 employees (152 temporary employees, not included in that figure), a decrease of 294 from the prior year (the annual securities report mainly attributes this to changes in production volume). Capital expenditure was ¥4,109 million.

entries.24ef8833c63a7405: This is a category handled by the company (H-ONE) itself, which manufactures and sells automotive parts in Japan. The company's principal facilities listed are the Kameyama Works (Kameyama, Mie Prefecture), the Maebashi Works (Maebashi, Gunma Prefecture) and the Development and Technology Center (Maebashi). Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥46,318 million (¥48,439 million in the prior year), and segment profit (operating profit) was ¥5,074 million (¥4,780 million in the prior year). Revenue from external customers declined, but intersegment internal revenue rose from ¥9,594 million to ¥17,578 million, so revenue including internal sales was ¥63,897 million, up 10.1% from the prior year. The company cites the increase in production of automobile frames for its main customers compared with the prior year and higher equipment sales as reasons, and explains that cost reductions in manufacturing from structural reforms reinforced the effect of higher revenue on profit. The breakdown of intersegment internal revenue is not described in the annual securities report. There are 1,023 employees (407 temporary employees, not included in that figure), a decrease of 118 from the prior year (the annual securities report mainly attributes this to staff reductions accompanying the consolidation of locations). Capital expenditure was ¥6,894 million. At the group level, the group mainly manufactures automobile body frames and sells them to several automakers and others, and its largest customer is [[company:honda|HONDA MOTOR CO., LTD.]] and its group companies. Revenue from that group was ¥186,344 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026 (¥199,868 million in the prior year), and the annual securities report explains that it accounts for about 90% of consolidated revenue. This amount is included in revenue from external customers across all four segments.

entries.c333b5de78d4d46f: This category manufactures and sells automotive parts through local subsidiaries in China. The consolidated subsidiaries are four companies: Guangzhou Aiji Auto Parts Co., Ltd. and Qingyuan Aiji Auto Parts Co., Ltd. in Guangdong Province, and Wuhan Aiji Auto Parts Co., Ltd. and Wuhan Aiji New Energy Vehicle Co., Ltd. in Hubei Province. Dongfeng Aiji Auto Press Parts Co., Ltd. in Hubei Province (ownership of voting rights 50.00%) is an associate accounted for under the equity method. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥32,431 million (¥38,557 million in the prior year), and segment profit (operating profit) was ¥3,143 million (¥2,352 million in the prior year). The company explains that, because production of automobile frames for its main customers fell from the prior year, revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥32,904 million, down 15.4% year on year; meanwhile, profit increased because the impairment loss temporarily recorded in the prior year (the prior-year impairment loss in China was ¥887 million) no longer applied, and because manufacturing costs were reduced through structural reforms, including a shift in production systems and consolidation of locations. Zhaoqing Aiji Auto Parts Co., Ltd. completed liquidation in December 2025 and was excluded from this category. There are 794 employees (170 temporary employees, not included in that figure), a decrease of 421 from the prior year (the annual securities report explains this mainly as corresponding to changes in production volume). Capital expenditure was ¥1,845 million.
entries.faa10af41835d12f: This [[term:segment|segment]] manufactures and sells automotive parts through local subsidiaries in the United States, Canada and Mexico. The [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] are five companies: KTH Parts Industries, Inc. (Ohio), Kalida Manufacturing, Inc. (Ohio), KTH Leesburg Products, LLC. (Alabama) and KTH Texas, Inc. (Ohio) in the United States, and KTH Shelburne Manufacturing, Inc. (Ontario) in Canada. G-ONE AUTO PARTS DE MEXICO, S.A. DE C.V. (Guanajuato) in Mexico is an equity-method affiliate. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥112,577 million (¥115,425 million in the prior year), the largest of the four reportable segments and more than half of consolidated revenue of ¥209,659 million. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥5,860 million (¥4,393 million in the prior year). The company explains that, because production of automobile frames for its main customers fell from the prior year due to the semiconductor supply shortage, revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥112,682 million, down 2.3% year on year; meanwhile, profit increased due to the effects of structural reforms, including streamlining and efficiency improvements of existing production lines and a major review of production patterns. KTH Texas, Inc. was established in August 2025 and joined the North American operations as a consolidated subsidiary from the third-quarter consolidated accounting period. There are 1,832 employees (439 temporary employees, not included in that figure), and capital expenditure for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥15,636 million.
